> Thanks! BTW did you measure the diff after this PR?

Yeah. But it seems that I can only remove some of the bytes. I am only able to drop a few module imports, which eliminates some `Object.defineProperty(t, "__esModule", { value: !0 })` and `("function" == typeof t.default || ("object" == typeof t.default && null !== t.default)) && void 0 === t.default.__esModule && (Object.defineProperty(t.default, "__esModule", { value: !0 }), Object.assign(t.default, t), (e.exports = t.default));`.

On the other hand, I do notice that there are some tree-shaking problems. E.g. the whole `next/navigation` is introduced to my bundle, while I don't use any of the Router API at all. I am going to work on that in my next PR.

body: Landed in #51851
author: timneutkens

body: To clarify after 2000 it will start using directory watches, on larger applications this causes a lot of file watcher closes which can take multiple seconds, on Vercel's application it took 6 to 8 seconds as macOS file watching is very slow to close. By reducing the limit it ensures directory watchers are always used instead, thus speeding up compilation by 6 to 8 seconds for this particular case.

body:
We are using standalone mode with appDirectory without any issues on 2 prod projects, as far as I know. The only issue we have is the server dying after some time due to OOM issues, but that's I think unrelated to standalone: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/45508

But please correct me if I am wrong and we should get rid of output: standalone
author: HamAndRock

body: It seems that this isn't just a problem with appDir, my project uses pageDir, but it's also has this problem
author: Innei

body: Yeah, I know. Just wanted to say that we use standalone mode without any problems with appDirectory. The OOM/crashes are not related to this issue.
author: HamAndRock

body:
Sorry if this is actually no longer the case, and standalone mode should work fine with the App router. I just ran into this when trying to use standalone mode for this template https://github.com/medusajs/nextjs-starter-medusa. I also tried to install `next@canary` and build, but get the same error.

So without standalone mode it works fine, but when I turn it on, I get this build error
```
> Build error occurred
[Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/Users/USERNAME/dev/nextjs-starter-medusa/.next/server/app'] {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ENOENT',
  syscall: 'lstat',
  path: '/Users/USERNAME/dev/nextjs-starter-medusa/.next/server/app'
}
```
author: bjornarhagen

body: Well I am just unsure, you get some weird errors on start but seems like it works fine in prod,
author: HamAndRock

body:
@bjornarhagen if you are using the `pages/` directory only, perhaps you can try setting `experimental.appDir` to false? Or add an `app/` page if there's none? Thanks!

[I added App Router support for `output: "standalone"` months ago](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/43367#issuecomment-1327960598), so the note added in this PR is not correct :)
author: DuCanhGH

body:
@DuCanhGH I see, must be something https://github.com/medusajs/nextjs-starter-medusa is doing that is causing the standalone build to fail then. Setting `experimental.appDir` to `false` does fix the issue.

Thank you so much! 😄
author: bjornarhagen

body: Note that the experimental flag is not needed with v13.4+.

Error 'Failed to download `Orbitron` from Google Fonts. Using fallback font instead.' I am on next: 13.4.7 node: 19.7.0 tailwind: 3.3.2 Complete error message: ``` [0] AbortError: The user aborted a request. [0] at abort (/project/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/node-fetch/index.js:1:65190) [0] at EventTarget.abortAndFinalize (/project/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/node-fetch/index.js:1:65410) [0] at [nodejs.internal.kHybridDispatch] (node:internal/event_target:758:20) [0] at EventTarget.dispatchEvent (node:internal/event_target:700:26) [0] at abortSignal (node:internal/abort_controller:314:10) [0] at AbortController.abort (node:internal/abort_controller:332:5) [0] at Timeout. (/project/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/@next/font/dist/google/fetch-font-file.js:24:51) [0] at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:568:17) [0] at process.processTimers (node:internal/timers:511:7) { [0] type: 'aborted' [0] } [0] - error Failed to download `Orbitron` from Google Fonts. Using fallback font instead. [0] - event compiled client and server successfully in 8.8s (475 modules) ``` app/layout.tsx ```jsx import { Orbitron } from "next/font/google"; const orbitron = Orbitron({ subsets: ["latin"], display: "swap", variable: "--font-orbitron", }); export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode; }) { return (
{children}
); } ``` The font preloading was working fine until I connected a fastAPI backend in my next project. After adding a basic get request to one of my server component the error surfaced. I tried reverting the component back my deleting the get request and deleting .next, node_modules and tried to re-run the app but still got the same error. Also the error only reproduces on the first render after deleting node modules. The browser console warning showed: ` The resource was preloaded using link preload but not used within a few seconds from the window's load event. Please make sure it has an appropriate 'as' value and it is preloaded intentionally next js ` ` The resource http://localhost:3000/_next/static/css/app/layout.css?v=1688126664983 was preloaded using link preload but not used within a few seconds from the window's load event. Please make sure it has an appropriate 'as' value and it is preloaded intentionally. ` The issue got resolved if I set preload:false to the font variable but is just a workaround I guess.
